skill.name: teach
skill.description: Builds a stateful teaching workspace with focused HTML lessons, curated resources, reusable references, and learning records tailored to the user's mission.
skill.summary: Create a structured, personalized learning program that preserves goals, resources, lessons, and demonstrated progress across sessions.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: All 21 static findings are false positives caused by inline code formatting, file paths, sample links, and ordinary teaching text. One separate medium-risk behavior remains: SKILL.md encourages an unspecified CLI command to open lesson files without explicit confirmation or command constraints.

remediation.issue: The lesson-opening instruction permits an unspecified CLI command.
remediation.suggestion: Use a platform-specific allowlist, pass only the generated lesson path, and require user confirmation before execution.

content.value_statement: Long-term learning loses context across separate AI sessions. This skill organizes goals, trusted resources, short HTML lessons, references, and progress records inside one workspace.
actual_capabilities: Captures a concrete learning mission, success criteria, constraints, and scope in MISSION.md.
Curates trusted knowledge sources and relevant communities in an annotated RESOURCES.md file.
Produces numbered, self-contained HTML lessons with focused explanations, practice, feedback, and citations.
Builds reusable lesson assets, concise reference documents, and a consistent topic glossary.
Records demonstrated understanding, corrected misconceptions, prior knowledge, and mission changes in sequential learning records.
Adapts the next lesson to the user's mission and recorded zone of proximal development.
limitations: Requires permission to create and update several files and directories in the current workspace.
Resource quality depends on available research tools and still requires user review.
Cannot independently prove mastery; it records evidence observed during interaction.
Opening an HTML lesson may invoke a platform-specific CLI command and should require user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Start a New Learning Goal
use_cases.description: Turn a broad topic into a concrete mission, trusted resource list, and first focused lesson.

use_cases.title: Learn a Technical Skill
use_cases.description: Build progressive lessons, reusable references, and practice loops around a programming or engineering objective.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Guided Curriculum
use_cases.description: Track demonstrated knowledge and adjust future lessons without repeating material the learner already understands.

prompt_templates.title: Define My Learning Mission
prompt_templates.prompt: Teach me {topic}. Ask why I need it, define observable success, identify constraints, and create the teaching workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Create My First Lesson
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my mission and current resources, create one short lesson on {subtopic} with practice, feedback, citations, and a tangible outcome.

prompt_templates.title: Continue From My Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my mission and learning records. Identify my current level, choose the next suitable skill, and build a lesson that avoids repetition.

prompt_templates.title: Refine the Learning System
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this teaching workspace for stale resources, duplicated assets, terminology conflicts, knowledge gaps, and unsupported learning records. Improve only confirmed issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced learner maintaining a mature workspace

output_examples.input: Teach me Rust so I can ship a reliable command-line tool for my team.
output_examples.output: Creates a mission with delivery criteria, curates primary Rust sources, and produces a short first lesson tied to the command-line project.

output_examples.input: Continue my strength-training lessons after I demonstrated that I understand progressive overload.
output_examples.output: Reviews the learning record, avoids reteaching the concept, and selects a more demanding lesson that fits the recorded goal.

output_examples.input: My goal changed from learning SQL syntax to analyzing product retention.
output_examples.output: Updates the mission after confirmation, records the change, and redirects resources and future lessons toward retention analysis.

best_practices: State a concrete real-world outcome before requesting the first lesson.
Review cited resources and generated lesson files before relying on them.
Demonstrate understanding through exercises so future lessons can adapt from evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated learning goals in one workspace.
Do not treat lesson coverage as proof that the learner understands the material.
Do not allow generated files or resource lists to grow without reviewing stale and duplicate content.

faq.question: Does this skill support learning across multiple sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It stores the mission, resources, lessons, references, preferences, and demonstrated progress in workspace files.

faq.question: What does the skill create?
faq.answer: It can create mission and resource documents, HTML lessons, reusable assets, reference pages, a glossary, notes, and learning records.

faq.question: How does it choose the next lesson?
faq.answer: It considers the mission, existing learning records, prior knowledge, and the learner's current level.

faq.question: Does it research external sources?
faq.answer: It directs the agent to find trusted sources and communities when suitable tools are available. Users should review every recommendation.

faq.question: Can it verify that I mastered a topic?
faq.answer: No. It can use exercises and observed responses as evidence, but it cannot independently certify mastery.

faq.question: Why does it need workspace access?
faq.answer: The skill preserves learning state by reading and updating local documents, lessons, assets, and progress records.
